Actors: UN Secretary-General António Guterres
Headline: UN Secretary General calls for global ceasefire
Information: On 23 March 2020, United Nations Secretary General António Guterres called for a global ceasefire to stop violent conflict in support of the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic.

Actors: UN Security Council (UNSC)
Headline: UN Security Council adopts resolution backing global ceasefire call
Information: More than three months after UN Secretary General (UNSG) Antonio Guterres called for a global ceasefire, the UN Security Council (UNSC) unanimously voted in favour of a resolution backing the call. The newly adopted Resolution 2530 (2020) stated that the UNSC's call upon conlict parties to engage in a "durable humanitarian pause", which should last for at least 90 days. Excluded from this call are operations  against Council-designated terrorist groups such as Da'esh, Al Qaeda and Al Nusra Front. UNSG GUterres welcomed the resolution and the UNSC's recognition of his appeal for a global ceasefire.

Region_entity: North, northeast and southwest Colombia and Venezuela border regions
Actors: National Liberation Army/Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN)
Headline: ELN announce unilateral ceasefire
Information: The National Liberation Army (ELN) announced a temporary unilateral ceasefire with the Colombian government on 29/03/2020, as "humanitarian gesture" in the face of COVID-19. The statement reserved the right of the ELN to defend itself against "attacks by state forces, made up of regular troops, paramilitaries and drug gangs in various regions of the country" and urged the Iván Duque governement to suspend military operations and to resume dialogue with ELN delegates in Cuba to agree on a bilateral and temporary cessation. The ELN also made other demands in the statement including the release of political prisoners, the free provision of the COVID-19 test kits and that "health must once again be an inalienable right, mandatory coverage by the State", among others.

Region_entity: North, northeast and southwest Colombia and Venezuela border regions
Actors: National Liberation Army/Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN)
Headline: ELN ceasefire commences
Information: The temporary unilateral ceasefire by the National Liberation Army (ELN) with the Colombian government, which was announced on 29/03/2020, commences. It was not reciprocated by the Colombian government. It was termed as "insufficient" by the Colombian government's High Commissioner for Peace Miguel Ceballos, who called for the ELN to “extend [its] terms indefinitely” and comply with the Government's set pre-conditions for resuming peace negotiations.

Region_entity: North, northeast and southwest Colombia and Venezuela border regions
Actors: National Liberation Army/Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN)
Headline: ELN announces ceasefire would not be extended
Information:
The National Liberation Army (ELN) published a statement on 27/04/2020 announcing that it would not extend its unilateral ceasefire and resume military operations on 01/05/2020. The group cited the "unfortunate" unreciprocated response from the Colombian government as the reason for not extending the ceasefire and accused the Colombian government of taking advantage of the unilateral cessation.

The Colombian government's High Commissioner for Peace Miguel Ceballos rejected the ELN’s decision, terming it as a "move away from the reality of the country" and demanded a permanent ceasefire, release of hostages and forcibly recruited minors, as well as a halt to anti-personnel mine installation. Ceballos had shown no interest in a bilateral ceasefire.
Media_credit: by KyleEJohnson, licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 2.0.

Region_entity: North, northeast and southwest Colombia and Venezuela border regions
Actors: National Liberation Army/Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN)
Headline: ELN adopts no-first-strike-policy for COVID-19 period
Information:
On 04/05/2020, the National Liberation Army (ELN) announced it would adopt a defensive strategy during the COVID-19 pandemic. Former peace negotiator Pablo Beltran, a member of the guerrilla group’s Central Command, said that following the one-month ceasefire that ended on 30/04/2020, the group “will not have attack plans, but defense plans.” ELN leadership also urged a bilateral ceasefire and called on the UN and Pope Francis to lobby for this with the Colombian government.

The focus of the High Commissioner for Peace is currently on promoting the individual demobilisation of ELN members, having passed a decree that allows members of illegal armed groups, including the ELN, to capitulate to the justice system and be allowed to take part in a reintegration program.The Commissioner reported that 20 ELN guerrillas had demobilized in the southwestern Cauca province at the beginning of May 2020.

Region_entity: North, northeast and southwest Colombia and Venezuela border regions
Actors: National Liberation Army/Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN)
Headline: ELN and Government discuss potential ceasefire
Information:
Head of negotiating team of the National Liberation Army (ELN), Pablo Beltrán, stated that the ELN would be willing to participate in a three-month global ceasefire that is being discussed at the United Nations to contain the spread of the coronavirus. He says that the group hopes that President Iván Duque will also support the cessation of hostilities.

President Duque demands from the ELN that a unilateral cessation of hostilities must include the suspension of kidnappings, the release of unlawfully detained prisoners, the commitment not to recruit minors and to abandon the use of antipersonnel mines.

Region_entity: North, northeast and southwest Colombia and Venezuela border regions
Actors: National Liberation Army/Ejército de Liberación Nacional (ELN)
Headline: ELN realeases six hostages in hope of resuming peace talks
Information: After two prisoners had been released on 12/06/2020, the rebel group National Liberation Army (ELN) freed another six hostages on 14/06/2020 amid pleas for the resumption of peace talks between the group and the Colombian government.
Media_credit: by Gwen Burnyeat, all rights reserved
Media_caption: School-Children in Pereira draw their hopes for peace, August 2016

Region_entity: North-West and South-West regions of Ambazonia/ Southern Cameroons
Actors: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF)
Headline: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces declare two-week ceasefire
Information:
The Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF), an Ambazonian separatist movement, declared a two-week ceasefire with the Cameroon government on 25/03/2020, announcing that the cessation of violence would "permit international humanitarian preparation for COVID-19 prevention". 
 
The Revolutionary High Command Council (REHCOCO) ordered all combat units of SOCADEF and its affiliates operating in nine of the thirteen counties of Ambazonia to stand down but to maintain positions with combat readiness to defend for 14 days. The statement also called on La Republique du Cameroun’s (LRC) forces to stand down or remain in position but not to attack Ambazonians.

Region_entity: North-West and South-West regions of Ambazonia/ Southern Cameroons
Actors: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF)
Headline: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces ceasefire commences
Information: The two-week ceasefire of the Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF) with the Cameroon government commences. It was declared on 25/03/2020. SOCADEF is the only separatist group (out of 15 groups) to have stopped fighting because of the pandemic in the North-West and South-West regions. The Ambazonia Governing Council, which is one of the biggest groups, said that a unilateral ceasefire would open the way for government troops to march unopposed into territory under its control. The Cameroonian government did not reciprocate the ceasefire, with clashes between military and separatists continuing throughout April.

Actors: Ambazonia Governing Council
Headline: Ambazonia Governing Council rejects unilateral ceasefire
Information: On 27/03/2020, a statement from Julius Nyiawung, the Vice President of the Ambazonia Governing Council, a separatist group claiming to be the legitimate government of the area, said there would not be a unilateral ceasefire. The Ambazonia Governing Council brings together several armed groups in the region.

Region_entity: North-West and South-West regions of Ambazonia/ Southern Cameroons
Actors: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF)
Headline: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces extend ceasefire
Information: The Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF) extended an initial two week ceasefire on 10/04/2020 to "permit additional international humanitarian preparation for COVID-19 preparation" and demanded that the Government of Cameroon respect the global ceasefire call by the UNSG. The statement made special mention of the plight of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and refugees, stating that 3 million Ambazonians fall under these categories. The statement also acknowledged the "imperfect" nature of the ceasefire, noting that SOCADEF has opened lines of communication with LRC field commanders to facilitate the ceasefire. The Commander-In-Chief of SOCADEF, Dr. Ebenzer Akwanga says he expects the extension would also give the International Committee of the Red Cross time to qualify the war in Southern Cameroons (Ambazonia) as a Non International Armed Conflict, NIAC.

Actors: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF)
Headline: Southern Cameroons Defence Forces extend ceasefire a second time
Information: On 25/04/2020, the Southern Cameroons Defence Forces (SOCADEF) announced another extension of its unilateral ceasefire.

Actors: Global Campaign for Peace and Justice
Headline: Nobel Prize laureates call for Cameroon ceasefire
Information: On 22/06/2020, the Global Campaign for Peace and Justice, "an informal group of academics, activists, journalists, lawyers, students, and other concerned citizens around the world", including Nobel Peace Prize laureates and former heads of states, called for a nationwide humanitarian ceasefire in Cameroon. The call addresses the national government and non-state armed groups, as well as the UN and regional organisations, such as the African Union, and implores all waring parties to put people's immediate health ahead of military objectives.

Actors: Republic of the Philippines
Headline: President Duterte declares unilateral ceasefire
Information: President Rodrigo Duterte declared a unilateral ceasefire with the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP) and its armed wing, the New People's Army (NPA), on 18/03/2020, effective from 19/03/2020 to 15/04/2020. Government forces were ordered to stop offensive operations against armed communist rebels so the state could focus on efforts to counter COVID-19. Presidential Spokesperson Salvador Panelo said the President directed the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) to issue the Suspension of Offensive Military and Police Operations (Somo) to implement the ceasefire.
Media_credit: by philwarren, licensed under CC BY 2.0

Actors: Republic of the Philippines
Headline: Government ceasefire commences
Information: A unilateral ceasefire of the Philippines Government with the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP) and its armed wing, the New People's Army (NPA) commences. It was declared on 18/03/2020, and is effective from 19/03/2020 to 15/04/2020. Both the police and the military welcomed the ceasefire, saying this would allow them to focus on responding to the threat of COVID-19 whilst remaining on defense.
Media_credit: by Judgefloro is licensed under CC0 1.0

Actors: Republic of the Philippines
Headline: Government announces ceasefire not to be extended
Information: On 18/04/2020, Government security forces announced the ceasefire would not be extended. Central Command chief Lt. Gen. Roberto Ancan said military operations against communist rebels in the Visayas had resumed on 16/04/2020. The Communist Party of the Philippines' armed wing, the New People's Army (CPP-NPA), accused the government of committing atrocities by launching 13 attacks between 16/03/2020 and 15/04/2020.

Actors: New People’s Army (NPA)/ Bagong Hukbong Bayan (BHB)
Headline: Communist Party of the Philippines orders its armed wing to observe ceasefire
Information: The Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP) ordered all commands and units of its armed wing, the New People’s Army (NPA), and the people’s militias to observe a nationwide ceasefire on 24/032020, aimed at both buying time for its forces and fighting COVID-19. However, the Armed Forces of the Philippines said it recorded NPA attacks against soldiers tapped to help in the government’s fight against COVID-19 even though the rebels extended the ceasefire.

Actors: New People’s Army (NPA)/ Bagong Hukbong Bayan (BHB)
Headline: Communist Party of the Philippines ceasefire commences
Information: A ceasefire by the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP) and its armed wing, the New People’s Army (NPA), and the people’s militias, commences. It was declared on 24/03/2020 and is set to be nationwide.The NPA's negotiating body, the National Democratic Front of the Philippines noted that its cessation of hostilities could be seen as a gesture of goodwill that could facilitate the resumption of peace negotiations.

Actors: New People’s Army (NPA)/ Bagong Hukbong Bayan (BHB)
Headline: Communist Party of the Philippines releases statement to uphold ceasefire
Information: On 30/03/2020, the New People’s Army (NPA), the armed wing of the opposition forces of the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP), released a supplementary statement to uphold the COVID-19 ceasefire of 24/03/2020.

Actors: New People’s Army (NPA)/ Bagong Hukbong Bayan (BHB)
Headline: Communist Party of the Philippines extends ceasefire for two more weeks
Information:
The Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP) extended the ceasefire until 30/04/2020 after President Duterte had prolonged the Luzon-wide quarantine to allow health authorities to conduct more coronavirus tests, “to ensure quick and unimpeded support to all people requiring urgent medical, health and socioeconomic assistance in the face of the public emergency over the COVID-19 pandemic.” It also reiterated the call for the “urgent release” of all political prisoners and for declaring a general amnesty and expressed desire for the resumption of the peace negotiations between the Government of the Republic of the Philippines (GRP) and the National Democratic Front of the Philippines (NDFP), which is the negotiating coalition of the CPP.

The Government cited a failure of the CPP and its armed wing, the New People's Army (NPA), to act in good faith as the main reason the ceasefire extension was not reciprocated.

Actors: New People’s Army (NPA)/ Bagong Hukbong Bayan (BHB)
Headline: New People's Army resumes military operations
Information: The New People’s Army (NPA) resumed operations after 26 days of ceasefire on 01/05/2020, stating that "the refusal of the Duterte regime to relent in its attacks against the NPA, despite calls for a “global ceasefire” has made the further extension of the NPA ceasefire impossible."

Actors: Chairs of Agatu, Etulo, Fulani, Hausa, Idoma, Igbo, Igede, Jukun, Tiv and Yoruba ethnic groups
Headline: Inter-communal ceasefire in Benue State
Information: An agreement to peaceful co-existence during and beyond the pandemic was signed by community leaders, youth groups and women leaders of 10 farmer-herder communities at a dialogue led by the organisation Humanitarian Dialogue (HD) to resolve the intercommunal farmer-herder conflict in Benue state in Nigeria. The Agreement aimed to allow for collective action against the pandemic and a resolution of the conflict and built on longer-term pre-COVID-19 negotiations.

Actors: Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N El Hilu faction)/ Harakat Al-Sha'abi Li-Tahrir Al-Sudan-Al-Shamal
Headline: Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North extends pre-COVID-19 ceasefire
Information: On 31/03/2020, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North faction led by Abdelaziz El Hilu (SPLM-N El Hilu) announced the extension of a pre-COVID-19 ceasefire (due to end on 31/03/2020) starting from 01/04/2020 until 30/05/2020. The movement said that the decision to extend the cessation of hostilities unilaterally in all areas under its control comes as a goodwill gesture and to give the ongoing peace talks in Juba an opportunity to succeed. The Sudanese government welcomed the extension and termed the unilateral truce as a "significant step" that demonstrated political will and a strong desire to achieve a and sustainable peace. Sovereign Council member and spokesman for the government’s negotiating delegation in Juba, Mohamed El Taayshi welcomed El Hilu’s statement and reiterated the government’s firm commitment to a comprehensive ceasefire in all regions of the Sudan that began on 16/10/2019. El Taayshi considered the extension of the cessation of hostilities an important step that demonstrates political will and a strong desire to achieve the comprehensive and sustainable peace that the Sudanese people deserve.

Actors: Sudan Liberation Movement/Army of Abdel Wahid al-Nur (SLM/A-AW)
Headline: Sudan Liberation Movement extends de-facto ceasefire
Information: On 31/03/2020, the Sudan Liberation Movement/Army of Abdel Wahid al-Nur (SLM/A-AW) accepted the UN’s calls for a ceasefire in Darfur but reiterated its rejection to join the peace process in Juba. The SLM stated it would continue to exercise a de facto ceasefire and not engage in offensive operations bar self-defence. Furthermore, leader Abdel Wahid al-Nur criticized the Hamdok government saying that it had no authority on the ground and that the power "remains in the hands of the leadership of the Sudanese Armed Forces" and the "Janjaweed genocidaire militias", rejecting the peace process and describing it as "a cosmetic exercise" to "legitimize a transitional government that lacks genuine sovereignty".

Actors: South Sudan Opposition Movements Alliance (SSOMA)
Headline: South Sudan Opposition Movements Alliance re-commits to existing ceasefire
Information: On 09/04/2020, the South Sudan Opposition Movements Alliance (SSOMA) renewed their commitment to the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement it signed in Rome on 12/01/2020 with the Government of South Sudan, reiterating its concern for the general safety of the South Sudanese people in the midst of COVID-19. SSOMA also committed to facilitate humanitarian access to South Sudan’s populations. The statement was made by the Leadership Council of SSOMA, comprising the leaders of 6 armed movements and political parties, namely the National Salvation Front (NAS), the South Sudan United Front (SSUF), the South Sudan National Movement for Change (SSNMC), the Real Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (R-SPLM), the National Democratic Movement Patriotic Front (NDM/PF) and the United Democratic Revolutionary Alliance (UDRA).

Actors: National Revolutionary Front/Barisan Revolusi Nasional Melayu Patan (BRN)
Headline: National Revolutionary Front declares ceasefire
Information: The National Revolutionary Front (BRN), the largest seperatist movement in Thailand's Deep South, declared a unilateral, open-ended ceasefire with the Thai Government on 03/04/2020 that would remain in force only for as long as the BRN was not attacked by government forces. It stated the ceasefire was intended to create a more stable environment for health workers. The ceasefire announcement was unprecedented in the history of the separatist insurgency. The Thai government did not reciprocate the ceasefire and continued its security operations. Maj. Gen. Pramote Prom-in, the Thai army’s regional spokesman dismissed the declaration as irrelevant to military efforts to curb violent activities in the southern border region. The Thai military said it would continue to “enforce laws on those who perpetrate against both officials and innocents ”and did not rule out anti-rebel operations.

Actors: National Revolutionary Front/Barisan Revolusi Nasional Melayu Patan (BRN)
Headline: National Revolutionary Front resumes military operations
Information: The National Revolutionary Front (BRN) announced a resumption of its operations After Thai security forces killed three BRN rebels on 30/04/2020 during a raid in in Nong Chik, Pattani. On 01/05/2020, the BRN released a written statement condemning the government's actions, whilst also publicly renewing its call for security forces to join its unilateral ceasefire. However, BRN fighters on the ground retaliated on 03/05/2020, shooting dead one paramilitary ranger and injuring another in Pattani province.

Actors: Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen
Headline: Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen declares ceasefires
Information: On 8 April 2020, the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Government of Yemen declared a unilateral ceasefire and stated that it wanted to support UN efforts for a political solution and help stop coronavirus spread. Saudi Arabia's state-run news agency SPA reported that the ceasefire was intended to help prevent a coronavirus outbreak in Yemen, while also allowing for a de-escalation in the fighting. Furthermore, it was aimed at giving the Houthis an opportunity to join UN-sponsored talks on a settlement to the conflict thousands of people. However, shortly afterwards it was reported that parties continued fighting despite the unilateral ceasefire, including Saudi airstrikes and Houthi-led advances and expansions in the North, which threatened one of the last government aligned strong holds, Marib.

Actors: Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen
Headline: Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen extends ceasefire
Information: On 24 April 2020, the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Government of Yemen announced a one-month extension of the ceasefire, reiterating that "the chance is still there for concerted efforts to reach a comprehensive and permanent ceasefire in Yemen". However, fighting between pro-government forces and Houthis had intensified in Northern Yemen despite the ceasefire and its extension, and there was fear that violence would escalate unless a nationwide ceasefire was agreed.
Media_credit: by Ibrahem Qasim, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0

Actors: Southern Transitional Council (STC), Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen
Headline: Bilateral ceasefire between STC and Yemeni Government agreed
Information: The Southern Transitional Council (STC) and the internationally recognized government of Yemen, agreed on a bilatreal ceasefire on 22/06/2020. The ceasefire applies to the Abyan province, which is a hotspot for fighting that the STC has partial control over, and also includes an agreement on the de-escalation in other regions and the resumption of peace talks between the two parties. The ceasefire aims to provide a basis for the implementation of the 2019 Riyadh peace agreement. In April, the STC had unilaterally declared self-rule in the southern region of Yemen, which had intensified existing tensions.
Media_credit: Image by kate nev is licensed under CC BY-NC 2.0

Actors: Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen
Headline: Yemeni Government deploys ceasefire observer troops
Information: On 24/06/2020, the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized Government of Yemen announced that it had deployed troops to observe and monitor the bilateral ceasefire from 22/06/2020 between the Yemeni government and the Southern Transtional Council (STC).
Media_credit: by TheMapLurker, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0
Media_caption: Yemen Warmap: Government (red), STC (yellow), Revolutionary Committee (green)

Actors: Southern Transitional Council (STC), Internationally Recognized Government of Yemen
Headline: Fighting in Southern Yemen continues despite ceasefire
Information: Despite a bilateral ceasefire between the internationally recognized Government of Yemen and the Southern Transtional Council (STC) that was declared on 22/06/2020, fighting between the two parties continued. Reportedly, on 25/06/2020 at least 54 people died as a result of these violent clashes.
Media_credit: by Ibrahem Qasim, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0

Actors: Movement of Democratic Forces in the Casamance
Headline: Movement of Democratic Forces in the Casamance calls on combatants to refrain from initiating attacks
Information:
The North-western, South-western and South-eastern fronts of the Movement of the Democratic Forces of Casamance (MFDC) have committed to fully cooperate with the Senegalese health authorities as well as humanitarian organisations to combat the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
In a Statement of solidarity of 16/04/2020, the MFDC also called on their combatants not to initiate military operations, to comply with the Geneva conventions, to facilitate emergency operations as well as to comply with and enforce the guidelines of health authorities.

Actors: Government of National Accord (GNA)
Headline: Government of National Accord endorses humanitarian ceasefire
Information: The UN-supported interim government of Libya, the Government of National Accord (GNA) under Prime Minister Fayez Sarraj, “endorsed an immediate humanitarian cessation of hostilities to allow local authorities to come together in response to the unprecedented public health challenge posed by COVID-19."

Actors: Libyan National Army (LNA)/ al-jaysh al-waṭaniyy al-Lībii
Headline: Libyan National Army commits to ceasefire
Information: Following the announcement of the internationally recognised Government of National Accord's (GNA), Major General Ahmed Mismari of the Libyan National Army (LNA), the GNA's subordinate armed forces, declared that the LNA would also commit to a ceasefire.

Actors: A thousand leading figures from across Libya
Headline: Civil Actors call for unity
Information: On 24 March 2020, a thousand leading figures in Libya signed a Call for Unity that urges Libyan actors and institutions to set aside anything other than truth and reason, and to stand united in the fights against COVID-19. Signatories included ome of Libya’s leading doctors, health professionals, mayors of towns and cities, parliamentarians and other political and media figures.

Actors: Libyan National Army (LNA)/ al-jaysh al-waṭaniyy al-Lībii
Headline: Libyan National Army declares unilateral ceasefire
Information: On 06/06/2020, Libyan National Army (LNA) commander Khalifa Haftar and the Egyptian president Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi presented the Cairo Declaration which  […] calls for respecting all international efforts and initiatives by declaring a ceasefire from 6pm [16:00 GMT] Monday, June 8, 2020".
Media_credit: by Ali Zifan,  licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0
Media_caption: June, 2020: Government of National Accord (green), Libyan National Army (red)

Actors: Libyan National Army (LNA)/ al-jaysh al-waṭaniyy al-Lībii
Headline: Libyan National Army ceasefire commences
Information: The unilateral ceasefire of the Libyan National Army (LNA) commences. It was declared by its commander Khalifa Haftar  on 06/06/2020.

Actors: Democratic Front of the Central African People/ Front démocratique du peuple centrafricain (FDPC)
Headline: Democratic Front of the Central African People recommits to existing peace deal
Information:
The Democratic Front of the Central African People (FDPC) committed to fully cooperate with health authorities, promote preventative measures against the virus and ensure the safety of humanitarian organisations.
The FDPC and the rebel group 'Return, Reclamation, Rehabilitation' (3R) are both signatories to the Political Agreement for Peace and Reconciliation (APPR) that officially ended the civil war in the Central African Republic on 05/02/2019. Their COVID-19 statements reaffirmed their commitment to peace during this turbulent period.

Actors: Return, Reclamation, Rehabilitation/ Retour, Réclamation, Réhabilitation (3R)
Headline: Rebel group 3R commits to promoting safety of humanitarian organisations
Information: 3R committed to fully cooperate with health authorities, promote preventative measures against the virus and ensure the safety of humanitarian organisations.

Actors: Movement of Central African Liberators for Justice (MLCJ)/ Le Mouvement des libérateurs centrafricains pour la justice
Headline: Movement of Central African Liberators for Justice guarantees safety of humanitarian organisations
Information: In a press release dated 04/05/2020, the Movement of Central African Liberators for Justice (MLCJ) pledged to promote pandemic prevention measures, fully cooperate with health authorities, as well as guarantee the safety of humanitarian organisations. MLCJ’s declaration follows those of the rebel group 'Retour, Réclamation, Réhabilitation' (3R) and the Democratic Front of the Central African People (FDPC). While technically a ceasefire had been called on 05/02/2019, this statement in-essence confirmed an ongoing commitment in the context of COVID-19.

Actors: Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF)/Quwwāt Sūriyā al-Dīmuqrāṭīya/ Hêzên Sûriya Demokratîk
Headline: Syrian Democratic Forces announce humanitarian truce
Information: The General Command of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) released a statement announcing the suspension of all SDF military activities other than self-defence in north-eastern Syria to allow warring parties to focus on their response to COVID-19 on 24/03/2020. SDF leadership urged all actors in Syria to refrain from military actions and make an immediate commitment to a humanitarian truce, “we hope that this humanitarian truce will help to open the door for dialogue and political solution and to put an end to the war in the world and Syria”. The SDF warned that a renewal of hostilities would increase the spread of the virus and severely affect Syria's deteriorated health infrastructure, already underequipped to handle the crisis.

Actors: Taliban
Headline: Taliban declare unilateral ceasefire during Eid
Information: On 23/05/2020 the Taliban unilaterally declared a three-day ceasefire for the period of Eid, starting on 24/05/2020.

Actors: Taliban
Headline: Taliban ceasefire commences
Information: A three-day ceasefire for the period of Eid by the Taliban commences. It was declared on 23/05/2020 and is set to end on 26/05/2020.

Actors: Afghan Government
Headline: Afghan government declares compliance with ceasefire
Information: The Afghan government welcomed the ceasefire declared by the Taliban on 23/05/2020 and instructed its troops to also comply.
Media_credit: NurPhoto/ Press Association. All rights reserved.

Actors: Afghan Government
Headline: Afghan government release prisoners in good faith
Information: On 26/05/2020 the Afghan Government released more than 900 prisoners in good faith and with the goal to get the Taliban to extend the ceasefire beyond the agreed three-day period.

Actors: Taliban
Headline: Taliban military operations recommence
Information: Skirmishes between Taliban fighters and Afghan security forces recommenced following the end of the three-day truce at midnight on 26/05/2020. The Afghan Ministry of Defence reported that on 28/05/2020 the Taliban killed at least 14 people from the security forces in northern Parwan and western Farah provinces. On 29/05/2020 members of the Afghan army were killed in the province of Paktiya. Three others were wounded in the attack that was also confirmed by the Taliban. The Afghan government is appealing to the Taliban to extend the ceasefire, stating that despite the latest attacks, a truce could still hold.

Region_entity: Shan state, Kachin state, China-Myanmar border
Actors: Northern Alliance
Headline: Northern Alliance declares month-long ceasefire
Information: The Northern Alliance, an alliance of ethnic armed groups, composed of the Arakan Army (AA), Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA), and Ta’ang National Liberation Army (TNLA), announced a unilateral ceasefire on 03/05/2020.

Region_entity: Nationwide excl. Rakhine state and Paletwa township of Chin state
Actors: Myanmar military (Tatmadaw)
Headline: Myanmar military announces 4-month ceasefire
Information: On 09/05/2020, the Myanmar military, the Tatmadaw, "issued a statement meeting the international standards to enforce a ceasefire in the areas from 10/05/2020 to 31/08/2020 except the areas where terrorist groups declared by the government take positions, with the aim of effectively and rapidly carrying out containment, prevention and treatment of COVID-19 in Myanmar and restoring eternal peace [...] The ceasefire left out Rakhine state and Paletwa township of Chin state, where clashes between the AA and the Myanmar military have been intensifying in recent weeks." Other regions included in the ceasefire declaration have also seen a resurgence of fighting."

Region_entity: Nationwide excl. Rakhine state and Paletwa township of Chin state
Actors: Myanmar military (Tatmadaw)
Headline: Myanmar military ceasefire commences
Information: A ceasefire of the Myanmar military, the Tatmadaw, set for the period between 10/05/2020 to 31/08/2020, commences. It was announced on 09/05/2020 with the aim to help with the containment of COVID-19 and to restore peace. It is not entirely nationwide as it does not extend to Rakhine state and Paletwa township of Chin state.

Actors: Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda (FLEC)
Headline: Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda declares 4-week ceasefire
Information: On 13/04/2020, the Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda (FLEC) declared a unilateral ceasefire starting on 13/04/2020 at 20:00 and lasting four weeks. The temporary ceasefire is a direct response to Guterres’ appeal for a global ceasefire, according to the FLEC spokesman Jean Claude Nzita.
Media_credit: by Goran tek-en, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0
Media_caption: Map or Cabinda region in Angola

Actors: Communist Party of India (CPI)
Headline: Communist Party of India announces unilateral ceasefire
Information: On 05/04/2020 the Communist Party of India (CPI), a Maoist communist party that mainly operates in the Red Corridor region of India, announced a unilateral ceasefire to help with containing the COVID-19 pandemic. With this, the CPI also gave a five-day deadline to the governments in the affected states to respond to the offer. In a statement, it said that the CPI, People’s Liberation Guerrilla Army (PLGA), which is its armed wing, and other frontal organisations "have decided against carrying out any kind of attack on the security forces during this period". This is, however, reliant on the government's compliance with the ceasefire and the PLGA reserved its right to resist if police initiated action. The declaration was not directly made by CPI leadership, but by the Malkangiri-Koraput-Visakha Divisional Committee (MKVDC), which is part of the CPI. The governmentdid not respond to this proposal.
